name: Saamia
sweep_summary: Saamia (saam1283) is not in the catalog. Of the three sweep items, two (Schwab & Dellwo 2017; Flege & Fletcher 1992) are Glottolog mis-assignments about Spanish stress perception and foreign accent, irrelevant; the third, Philippson 1991 (Tons et accent..., 542-pp Paris V thesis linked by Glottolog to 48 languages incl. Saamia), is print-only (theses.fr 'accessible: non', not on HAL) and its abstract describes the tone-to-penultimate-accent continuum of East African Bantu without placing Saamia. Beyond the title list, the language's Glottolog bibliography and the IULC Working Papers archive yielded open texts that were fetched sources and read but are silent on word stress (Marlo 2019 Saamia NC phonology; Hieda 2016 AALL 10; Marlo 2008 Tura, which groups Saamia among predictable-tone Luyia dialects), plus the abstract of Marlo & Brown 2002 'Segmental duration in Lusaamia', which explicitly tests the Bantu penultimate-stress expectation acoustically but whose PDF is not attached (old IULC site gone; web.archive.org unreachable from our machine). Print/search-only leads with the best chance of a stress statement: Botne, Ochwada & Marlo 2006 grammatical sketch (HathiTrust search-only; Harvard print), Chagas 1976 and Poletto 1998 (tonal studies). No best_new_statement; no catalog change.fr, HAL, CiNii, TUFS, ScholarWorks IU and SAL.

sources.quote: There is relatively little prior research on Saamia. The main works describing aspects of the structure of Saamia are Chagas (1976), Poletto (1998), Marlo (2002, 2004, 2006), Marlo & Brown (2002), Botne (2004), Botne et al. (2006), and Heida (2016).
sources.note: Read in full. Describes 1SG N- prefix allomorphy before stems (NC phonology); explicitly '(Tone is not transcribed.)'; no mention of stress, accent or penultimate length. Useful only for its literature summary: 'The main works describing aspects of the structure of Saamia are Chagas (1976), Poletto (1998), Marlo (2002, 2004, 2006), Marlo & Brown (2002), Botne (2004), Botne et al. (2006), and Heida (2016).'

sources.quote: Besides segmental effects on other segments, this paper also touches on the effects of position and stress on vowel length within a given utterance. [...] Mean durations of pre-antepenultimate and penultimate position of the infinitival form of reduplicated CVC verbs are discussed. Since stress is claimed to be penultimate in many Bantu languages, one might expect penultimate vowels to be longer than vowels in other positions (Batibo 2000, Anyanwu 2001). This hypothesis is considered in light of the acoustic measurements.
sources.note: Abstract only (ScholarWorks lists the article but attaches no PDF galley; the old indiana.edu/~iulcwp site is gone and web.archive.org is unreachable from our machine). The abstract states that the paper measures penultimate vs. other-position vowel duration in CVC and reduplicated CVCV infinitives and tests the Bantu penultimate-stress expectation acoustically — the body presumably reports whether Lusaamia penultimate vowels are longer. Best candidate for a first-hand, instrumental statement on Saamia word-level prominence.

sources.quote: Ces systèmes varient en effet depuis des langues pleinement tonales (kikuyu) jusqu'à des langues à accent démarcatif pénultième (swahili), tous les cas intermédiaires étant représentés. [...] on propose l'hypothèse que le moteur principal de l'évolution des systèmes concernés a été l'émergence d'un accent démarcatif sur la pénultième servant de limite de domaine pour l'association tonale.
sources.note: Only the theses.fr record was reachable (API record saved; field "accessible": "non"; not on HAL, not on archive.org). Glottolog links the thesis to 48 languages including Saamia. Abstract (EN): 'We find at one end purely tonal systems (like kikuyu) and at the other end systems with purely demarcative penultimate stress, with all intermediate cases... a hypothesis is presented according to which the emergence of penultimate accent is the main cause of the evolution of these systems.' The abstract does not say where Saamia sits on that continuum; whether the body contains a Saamia-specific acc…
